newsitem.title: USA: AT&T sees competition hurting second half.
newsitem.headline: AT&T sees competition hurting second half.

text.p: AT&T Corp, citing competition in its key long-distance telephone business, said third quarter earnings could be as much as 10 percent below analysts' estimates and that the pressure will continue, hurting fourth quarter profits.

In a press release, AT&T Chairman Robert Allen said Q3 results appear to be as much as 10 percent below analysts' mean estimate of $0.92 per share and that the fourth quarter will likely fall short of the mean estimate of $0.89 per share.
Allen also said earnings are being hurt by investment in local, on-line and wireless services as well as infrastucure to provide new communications and information services.

In another announcement earlier Tuesday, the company took aim at competitors with a new long-distance calling plan that would give consumers the option of a flat, calling rate of $0.15 per minute at any time, to anywhere in the U.S.
"Further, we currently believe that competitive pressures will continue for the remainder of the year, and we are intensifying our marketing efforts," Allen said in a statement.
AT&T stock fell 3-1/4 points to 54 in pre-opening trade on the New York Stock Exchange. The stock is poised to drop enough that it could take almost 20 points off the Dow Jones Industrial Average.
Allen said the fourth quarter per-share result would fall short of the $0.89 estimate by the same amount as the third quarter, or 10 percent.
The company said the per-share estimates from key analysts that follow the company for the third and fourth quarters were for continuing operations.
AT&T reported a profit of $0.90 a share on operations, or a net of $0.16, in last year's third quarter. Those results followed a restructuring charge for the NCR Corp unit ahead of its spinoff.
The company also had per-share earnings of $0.94 a share on operations in the fourth quarter of 1995, with a loss of $1.67 a share following a $4 billion restructuring charge.
Allen said the company had been hurt by competition from other long-distance telephone companies.
"While we have succeeded in stabilizing volumes and revenues at last quarter's levels, the number of customers moving between carriers is still disturbing."
He added, "Our research indicates that this customer volatility is due largely to price misperceptions that are frequently promoted by some competitors."

The announcment of a fall in earnings comes as AT&T finishes shedding some of its subsidiaries as part of a restructuring. AT&T will complete the spinoff of its Lucent Technologies Inc unit on Sept 30.

Allen also said the company would file registration documents with the Securities and Exchange Commission by the the end of the month for distribution of NCR stock to AT&T shareholders by the end of the year.
"Finally, we expect to complete the sale of Capital Corp to a group of its managers and outside investors in October, possibly as early as next week," he said.
